steps.title: Apply online for your study permit (your eTA comes with the approval)
steps.why: You need a study permit to study at UBC, and as a citizen of a visa-exempt country you need an electronic travel authorization (eTA) rather than a visitor visa to fly to Canada. When IRCC approves a study permit applied for from outside Canada, they send a port of entry letter of introduction and also issue the eTA — the letter of introduction includes your eTA information, so you don't apply separately or pay another fee. Your eTA is linked to the passport you used to apply and is valid for 5 years or until that passport expires, whichever comes first, so you must travel with that same passport. Note the letter of introduction is not your study permit: bring it and show it to a border services officer, who issues the permit at the port of entry.
prerequisites: Valid passport (the one you will travel with — your eTA gets linked to it)
Letter of acceptance from UBC
An IRCC secure account (used to pay fees, submit the application and check status)
A scanner or camera to make electronic copies of your documents
A valid credit or debit card (Canadian bank INTERAC Online registered for online banking, or any Visa Debit card; the card does not have to be in your name)
Your local visa office instructions for the country/territory you're applying from, plus proof of enough money for your stay
steps.cost: Study permit application fees paid online by credit/debit card in your IRCC account; no separate application or fee for the eTA
steps.time_estimate: Processing times vary by country — apply as early as possible and track status in your IRCC account

steps.title: Book and give your biometrics within 30 days of the BIL
steps.why: IRCC collects biometrics (fingerprints and photo) for most study permit applications to confirm your identity and help assess your application. After you apply, you'll get a biometrics instruction letter — you have 30 days to give your biometrics, and booking your collection appointment as soon as you can avoids processing delays. Biometrics are valid for 10 years, making repeat trips to Canada easier.
prerequisites: Submitted study permit application online (with letter of acceptance and PAL/TAL)
Paid the biometrics fee at the time you submitted your application
Received the letter from IRCC telling you to give biometrics
steps.cost: CAN$85 per applicant; maximum CAN$170 for families applying at the same time (spouse/common-law partner and dependent children)
steps.time_estimate: Book immediately; must be completed within 30 days of receiving the biometrics instruction letter

steps.title: Check your assessed fees in Workday and arrange your international payment in time for the Term 1 deadline
steps.why: Once your fees are assessed, the exact amount owing appears under "Finances" in Workday — that is the figure your bank transfer must match. Term 1 tuition fees for the Winter Session are due September 9, 2026 (the first instalment covers Term 1 courses, the first half of two-term courses, and most student fees), so initiating a bank wire or transfer service a few business days ahead of the deadline keeps you clear of late payment. Because your currency corridor is a major, liquid one, a standard bank wire or transfer service should settle with short lead times. Note that your temporary iMED medical insurance fee is charged to your account when you register for courses, and residence/meal plan instalments are paid separately through the UBC Student Housing and Community Services online service centre — budget for these alongside tuition.
prerequisites: Accepted your offer of admission and paid the acceptance deposit (paid online through the Applicant Service Centre)
Registered for your courses so fees can be assessed
Access to Workday to view your assessed fees under "Finances"
Standard proof-of-funds documentation prepared (no additional country-specific requirements apply to you)
steps.cost: Varies by program — use the UBC cost estimator for an estimate before your fees are assessed; iMED temporary medical insurance is $237 (or $338 for one-term exchange students) plus a $10.54 direct billing fee. Sending bank or transfer-service fees are additional.
steps.time_estimate: 30–60 minutes to confirm the amount in Workday and initiate the transfer; allow several business days for funds to settle before the due date

steps.title: Prepare your port-of-entry documents for arrival in Canada
steps.why: Your study permit is issued at the border, not before you fly. A border services officer will check that you meet entry requirements and will use the permit reference number on your port of entry letter of introduction to print your study permit. If you need an eTA, it's linked electronically to the passport you used for your study permit application — there's no visa sticker to show — so travelling with a different passport can cause serious problems at the border.
prerequisites: Approved study permit application with a port of entry letter of introduction received from the visa office
The same passport (or other valid travel document) you used to apply for your study permit
Valid letter of acceptance from your UBC (your designated learning institution)
If applicable: valid eTA (linked to your passport), valid visitor visa/temporary resident visa in your passport, or valid green card plus passport of nationality if you're a US permanent resident
steps.time_estimate: 1–2 hours to gather and organize documents; expect additional time with a border services officer on arrival

steps.title: Apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN) with Service Canada
steps.why: A SIN is the 9-digit number Service Canada issues that you need to start working in Canada, file taxes, and access government programs — and UBC requires it for tax purposes. As a grad student likely to hold a TA or RA appointment, apply as soon as you can: online applications may take up to 5 business days and mail up to 20, while an in-person appointment gets you the SIN during your visit. International students receive a SIN starting with "9", indicating temporary resident status. Once you have applied and meet the work eligibility requirement, you can work in insurable employment (work under an employer in Canada who controls your wages, hours, and tasks). Add your SIN in Workday once received, and protect it — it is sensitive personal information, and government-impersonation scam calls and emails are common.
prerequisites: Arrive in Canada and receive your study permit at the airport or border crossing — international students can only apply after arrival

Check your study permit lists a work condition, e.g. "May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186(f), (v) or (w)...", "May work 24 hours per week off campus or full time during regular breaks...", or "May accept employment on the campus of the institution at which registered in full-time studies"
If your permit has no work conditions (e.g. you previously studied at a secondary school), apply to change your study permit conditions first and apply for a SIN after receiving the new permit
A copy of your passport in addition to your study or work permit; certified translation if a document is not in English or French
Confirm you are otherwise eligible to work in Canada — a SIN alone is not enough
steps.time_estimate: Application takes under an hour online; up to 5 business days for online processing, up to 20 business days by mail, or same-visit if applying in person

steps.title: Apply for B.C. Medical Services Plan (MSP) as soon as you arrive in B.C.
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in MSP to access provincial health care benefits like doctor visits, and UBC notes you are required by BC law to register for MSP if you do not have other medical coverage. If you are new to Canada, apply as soon as you arrive: coverage may start three months after your arrival date in British Columbia (the wait period is the balance of the month in which you establish residence, plus two months). Because of that gap, you should get private health care insurance while you wait — UBC's schedule notes that if you arrived in August, your waiting period will likely be over in November. You can apply online (the easiest and fastest way), in person, or by mail; check the ID requirements before you start. Completing MSP enrolment gets you a B.C. Services Card and your Personal Health Number (PHN). Note: coverage depends on residency — if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses.
prerequisites: Arrival in British Columbia (apply as soon as you arrive)
ID meeting MSP's ID requirements
Private health insurance arranged to cover the three-month wait period
steps.cost: MSP premiums listed by UBC: $0 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents; $75/month for students on a study permit. Private interim coverage during the wait period is an additional cost.
steps.time_estimate: Apply on arrival; coverage may begin about three months after your arrival date in B.C.

steps.title: Check your MSP application status and plan for the 3-month wait period
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP) to access provincial health benefits like doctor visits. If you are new to Canada, coverage does not start right away: new residents may be eligible only after a wait period consisting of the balance of the month in which residence is established, plus two months — so coverage may start about three months after your arrival date in B.C. Following up now confirms your application is being processed and reminds you to hold private health insurance for the gap. Note that if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses.
prerequisites: An MSP Application for Enrolment already submitted online, in person or by mail
Your arrival date in B.C. (this is when the wait period is calculated from)
Private health care insurance arranged to cover you during the wait period (or, if you moved from another province, continued coverage under your former provincial medical plan)
If your coverage will be under an employer, union or pension group plan, your group administrator's contact details
steps.cost: No cost to apply or to check your application status
steps.time_estimate: 15–30 minutes to follow up; coverage typically begins about 3 months after your arrival date in B.C.
